claim: AWS Artifact provides on-demand downloads of AWS security and compliance documents, such as ISO and PCI compliance reports and SOC reports, and certifications from accreditation bodies.
question: Where do you download AWS's own SOC, PCI or ISO reports?

values.display: on-demand downloads of AWS security and compliance documents
System and Organization Controls (SOC) reports

evidence.quote: AWS Artifact provides on-demand downloads of AWS security and compliance documents. For example, reports on compliance with International Organization for Standardization (ISO) standards and Payment Card Industry (PCI) Security Standards, and System and Organization Controls (SOC) reports.

claim: With AWS Artifact you review, accept and track the status of your agreements with AWS for one account or for multiple accounts in your organization; with AWS Organizations, an agreement such as a BAA accepted for the organization automatically covers all existing and later member accounts.
question: How do you accept the HIPAA BAA for every account in an organization, including future accounts?

values.display: review, accept, and track the status of your agreements
on behalf of all AWS accounts in your organization
All existing and subsequent member accounts are automatically covered

qualifiers.scope: per AWS account or per organization

evidence.quote: Additionally, you can use AWS Artifact to review, accept, and track the status of your agreements with AWS for your AWS account and for multiple AWS accounts in your organization.

If you use AWS Organizations, you can accept agreements, such as a BAA with AWS, on behalf of all AWS accounts in your organization. All existing and subsequent member accounts are automatically covered by the agreement and can legally process PHI.

claim: Companies subject to HIPAA typically need a Business Associate Addendum (BAA) with AWS to safeguard protected health information; in the AWS Artifact console you review and accept such agreements and designate an account that can legally process PHI.
question: Which AWS Artifact agreement does a HIPAA workload usually need?

values.display: a Business Associate Addendum (BAA) agreement with AWS
designate an AWS account that can legally process PHI

qualifiers.scope: per AWS account or per organization

evidence.quote: For example, companies that are subject to the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) typically require a Business Associate Addendum (BAA) agreement with AWS to ensure that protected health information (PHI) is appropriately safeguarded. In the AWS Artifact console, you can review and accept such agreements, and you can designate an AWS account that can legally process PHI.

claim: You can use AWS Artifact to confirm that an agreement is accepted, review its terms, terminate it when no longer needed, and activate it again later.
question: Can an accepted AWS Artifact agreement be terminated and reactivated?

values.display: use AWS Artifact to terminate the agreement
you can activate the agreement again

evidence.quote: If your account or organization no longer needs to use an accepted agreement, then you can use AWS Artifact to terminate the agreement. If you terminate the agreement but later realize that you need it, then you can activate the agreement again.

claim: AWS Artifact documents demonstrate the security and compliance of the AWS infrastructure and services you use; you submit them to auditors or regulators as audit artifacts, while you remain responsible for documents that demonstrate your own company's security and compliance.

values.display: the security and compliance of the AWS infrastructure and services that you use
submit AWS Artifact documents to your auditors or regulators

within your company, with your regulators, and with your auditors
